headline: High-risk default interaction: Open Interpreter can read/write the filesystem and execute code, while LlamaFactory is a non-isolated local agent with no shared-channel protections.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter can read files and process clipboard/stdin, so attacker-controlled content from LlamaFactory outputs could be treated as instructions if manually bridged. LlamaFactory itself has no shared channel or parser protections, but the pair still has a plausible manual-copy or file-based injection path.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory output is copied into Open Interpreter prompts or files
IF Open Interpreter is run with clipboard or stdin/stdout as an input bridge
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Use a plain-text delimiter template for copied outputs
Review any copied LlamaFactory output before pasting
Keep Open Interpreter in confirmation mode, not --auto_run
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the entire local filesystem and has broad network egress, while LlamaFactory is a local open-source agent with no stated isolation. If LlamaFactory touches sensitive local files or secrets, Open Interpreter can ingest them and potentially transmit them to configured model providers or other endpoints.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present on the local machine
IF Open Interpreter is configured to send prompts or file contents to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Restrict Open Interpreter to a dedicated non-sensitive directory
Remove secrets from the local workspace before running the pair
Disable or minimize external model-provider usage
Run Open Interpreter in experimental Docker mode
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification capabilities, while LlamaFactory is not writable or executable itself but can still be used as an upstream producer of commands or files. The shared filesystem concurrency model in Open Interpreter makes concurrent writes and git-state conflicts plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same working directory
IF either agent writes generated artifacts that the other later edits or commits
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes to shared files
Avoid git operations from both agents in the same repo
Use file snapshots before handoff
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can execute actions after receiving text, and LlamaFactory can generate outputs that may be treated as authoritative instructions or facts. Without a verification layer, errors from LlamaFactory can cascade into Open Interpreter’s code execution and filesystem actions, creating irreversible downstream changes.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes LlamaFactory output as task instructions or facts
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to execute code after that handoff
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Separate fact generation from action execution
Use a validation checklist for any generated commands
Keep Open Interpreter confirmation prompts enabled
requires-engineering: add structured verification between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine and can send context to configured model providers, while LlamaFactory is an open-source local agent with no documented residency or retention controls here. The pair can therefore move local sensitive data into external processing paths, but the exact compliance breach depends on what data is present and which provider is configured.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is present on the local machine
IF Open Interpreter is configured with a non-compliant external model provider
mitigations: Avoid regulated data on the host
Use only approved model providers
Review retention settings before use
Run in a segregated environment
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
